title: BECE Nigeria
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public BECE junior secondary syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: Amina read in the notice that her school would close early because the well in the compound had dried up and there was no water for the pupils. Why would the school close early?
options: Because the school well had dried up and there was no water
Because the pupils had finished their examinations
Because a public holiday had been announced
Because the teachers were travelling to a workshop
items.explanation: The notice states that the well dried up and there was no water for the pupils, so the school closed early for lack of water; the other reasons are not mentioned in the passage.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - English Studies

items.stem: Choose the word that is nearest in meaning to the word 'diligent' as used in this sentence. The diligent pupil always finished her homework on time.
items.explanation: Diligent means hardworking and careful, so a diligent pupil works steadily and finishes on time; lazy and careless are its opposites.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - English Studies

items.stem: Choose the word that is most nearly opposite in meaning to the word 'scarcity' in this sentence. There was scarcity of water during the dry season.
items.explanation: Scarcity means a shortage or lack of something, so its opposite is abundance; shortage and drought are close in meaning to scarcity rather than opposite to it.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - English Studies

items.stem: Fill the gap with the correct option. The pupils were happy ____ they had all passed the promotion examination.
items.explanation: Because introduces the reason for their happiness, so it correctly links the feeling to its cause in this sentence.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - English Studies

items.stem: In the expression 'to bite the bullet', the speaker means to
items.explanation: To bite the bullet is an idiom meaning to face a painful or difficult situation with courage, not a literal act of biting anything.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - English Studies

items.stem: Which of the following words has its primary stress on the second syllable?
items.explanation: Begin is stressed on the second syllable, beGIN, while teacher, market and table are all stressed on the first syllable.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - English Studies

items.stem: Fill the gap with the correct option. Neither the monitor nor the prefects ____ present at the assembly.
items.explanation: With neither and nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, prefects, which is plural, so the correct form is were.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - English Studies

items.stem: Fill the gap with the correct option. The teacher asked the pupils to put ____ their books and listen carefully.
items.explanation: The phrasal verb put away means to place something where it belongs, which fits the instruction to keep the books aside.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - English Studies

items.stem: Which of the following sentences is correctly punctuated?
options: My mother said, 'Come home early today.'
My mother said 'come home early today'.
My mother said, come home early today.
My mother said come home early today.
items.explanation: A direct quotation is separated from the reporting words by a comma and enclosed in quotation marks, with the full stop inside the closing mark.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - English Studies

items.stem: Choose the option that correctly completes this sentence. She has been living in Enugu ____ 2019.
items.explanation: Since is used with a point in time such as 2019, while for is used with a period of time such as five years.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - English Studies

items.stem: Choose the word that is nearest in meaning to the word 'brave' in this sentence. The brave girl rescued her brother from the fire.
items.explanation: Brave means showing courage in the face of danger, so courageous is the nearest synonym; fearful and weak are opposites.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - English Studies

items.stem: Choose the word that is most nearly opposite in meaning to the word 'ancient' in this sentence. They visited the ancient city of Kano.
items.explanation: Ancient means very old, so its opposite is modern; old and historic are close in meaning to ancient rather than opposite.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - English Studies

items.stem: Fill the gap with the correct option. The news ____ surprising to everybody in the village that morning.
items.explanation: News is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb, so the correct form is was.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - English Studies

items.stem: In the sentence 'The test was a piece of cake', the expression a piece of cake means that the test was
items.explanation: A piece of cake is an idiom meaning something very easy, not a literal piece of food.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - English Studies

items.stem: Read the passage and answer the question that follows. Okon carried his lamp through the dark bush until he reached the stream, then he sat quietly and waited for the fish. What did Okon do when he reached the stream?
options: He called out loudly for help
He sat quietly and waited for the fish
He put out his lamp and slept
items.explanation: The sentence states that he sat quietly and waited for the fish at the stream, so that is exactly what he did next.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - English Studies

items.stem: A trader bought a basket of tomatoes for N1,200 and later sold it for N1,500. What was the trader's profit?
items.explanation: Profit is the selling price minus the cost price, so N1,500 minus N1,200 equals N300.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Simplify the sum of one half and one third and give the answer in its lowest terms.
items.explanation: The lowest common denominator is six, so one half becomes three sixths and one third becomes two sixths, giving five sixths.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Find the value of x in the equation 3x + 4 = 19.
items.explanation: Subtracting four from both sides gives 3x = 15, so x = 15 divided by 3 = 5.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: What is the area of a rectangle that is 8 centimetres long and 5 centimetres wide?
items.explanation: The area of a rectangle is length times width, so 8 centimetres times 5 centimetres equals 40 square centimetres.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Express the fraction three quarters as a percentage.
items.explanation: Three quarters multiplied by one hundred percent equals seventy-five percent.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Find the simple interest on N5,000 for 2 years at 10 percent per annum.
items.explanation: Simple interest equals principal times rate times time divided by one hundred, giving 5000 times 10 times 2 divided by 100 = N1,000.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: The angles of a triangle are 60 degrees, 50 degrees and x degrees. What is the value of x?
items.explanation: The three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees, so x = 180 - 60 - 50 = 70.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Simplify 2 raised to the power 3 multiplied by 2 raised to the power 2.
items.explanation: Adding the indices gives 2 raised to the power 5, and two multiplied by itself five times equals 32.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Find the average of the numbers 4, 6, 8 and 10.
items.explanation: The average is the sum of the numbers divided by how many there are, so 4 + 6 + 8 + 10 = 28 and 28 divided by 4 = 7.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3 to 2. If there are 30 pupils in the class, how many are boys?
items.explanation: The total ratio is 5 parts, and 30 divided by 5 is 6, so the number of boys is 3 times 6 = 18.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Find the highest common factor of 12 and 18.
items.explanation: The factors common to 12 and 18 are 1, 2, 3 and 6, and the highest of these is 6.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: A fair die is thrown once. What is the probability of obtaining an even number?
items.explanation: The even numbers on a die are 2, 4 and 6, giving three favourable outcomes out of six, so the probability is three sixths, which is one half.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Solve the equation x divided by 4 equals 7.
items.explanation: Multiplying both sides of the equation by 4 gives x = 7 times 4 = 28.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: The perimeter of a square is 36 centimetres. What is the length of one side?
items.explanation: A square has four equal sides, so the length of one side is 36 divided by 4 = 9 centimetres.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Express the decimal number 0.25 as a fraction in its lowest terms.
items.explanation: 0.25 is twenty-five hundredths, and dividing the numerator and denominator by 25 gives one quarter.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: A pupil pours water into a glass, then adds sand and stirs the mixture. Which method is best for separating the sand from the water?
items.explanation: Sand does not dissolve in water, so filtration using filter paper separates the solid sand from the liquid water.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Basic Science and Technology

items.stem: Green plants make their own food using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide. What is this process called?
items.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make their own food.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Basic Science and Technology

items.stem: A boy pushes a heavy box across the classroom floor but the box does not move. Which force opposes the motion of the box?
items.explanation: Friction between the base of the box and the floor opposes the push, so the heavy box does not slide.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Basic Science and Technology

items.stem: Which of the following materials is a good conductor of electricity?
items.explanation: Copper is a metal with free electrons, so it conducts electricity well, while wood, rubber and plastic are insulators.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Basic Science and Technology

items.stem: A student dissolves salt in a beaker of water until no more salt will dissolve at room temperature. The solution is said to be
items.explanation: A saturated solution is one that can no longer dissolve more solute at that temperature, so the extra salt settles at the bottom.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Basic Science and Technology

items.stem: Which organ of the human body pumps blood to all parts of the body?
items.explanation: The heart is a muscular organ that pumps blood through the blood vessels to all parts of the body.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Basic Science and Technology

items.stem: The part of a plant that absorbs water and mineral salts from the soil is the
items.explanation: Roots absorb water and dissolved mineral salts from the soil, and these are then carried up the stem to the rest of the plant.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Basic Science and Technology

items.stem: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
items.explanation: Solar energy comes from the sun and is naturally replaced, while coal, petroleum and natural gas are non-renewable fossil fuels.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Basic Science and Technology

items.stem: When a magnet is suspended freely it always comes to rest pointing in the north-south direction. This shows that the earth behaves like a
items.explanation: A freely suspended magnet aligns itself with the earth's magnetic field, which shows that the earth itself acts like a giant magnet.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Basic Science and Technology

items.stem: A pupil lifts a heavy stone using a long iron bar resting on a small stone as a pivot. The iron bar is an example of a
items.explanation: A rigid bar that turns about a fixed point called a fulcrum is a lever, which is one of the simple machines.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Basic Science and Technology

items.stem: Which of the following is a function of the white blood cells in the human body?
items.explanation: White blood cells defend the body by engulfing germs and producing antibodies, while red blood cells carry oxygen and platelets help clotting.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Basic Science and Technology

items.stem: The change of water vapour into liquid water when it cools is called
items.explanation: Condensation is the change of a gas or vapour into a liquid on cooling, as when water droplets form on a cold glass.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Basic Science and Technology

items.stem: A balanced diet contains all the food nutrients in the correct proportions. Which nutrient is mainly needed for body growth and repair?
items.explanation: Proteins are body-building foods needed for growth and for the repair of worn-out tissues.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Basic Science and Technology

items.stem: Which of the following devices is used to store programs and data in a computer?
items.explanation: The hard disk is a storage device that keeps programs and data even when the computer is switched off.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Basic Science and Technology

items.stem: A farmer notices that his maize plants are being eaten by insects. Which of the following is the best way to protect the crops?
options: Apply the recommended insecticide to the crops
Pour hot water on the whole farm
Remove all the leaves from the plants
items.explanation: Applying the recommended insecticide controls the insect pests, while the other actions would harm the crops rather than protect them.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Basic Science and Technology

items.stem: A group of people living together in a community share the same customs, language and values. This type of group is best described as a
items.explanation: A society is a group of people living together and sharing common customs, language, values and institutions.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Social Studies and Civic Education

items.stem: Which of the following is a duty of a good citizen in a democratic society?
options: Obeying the law and paying taxes
items.explanation: Good citizens obey the law and pay their taxes, which provide the revenue government uses to serve the people.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Social Studies and Civic Education

items.stem: The body of rules by which a country is governed is called the
items.explanation: A constitution is the body of fundamental laws that states how a country is governed and the rights of its citizens.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Social Studies and Civic Education

items.stem: A family made up of a father, a mother and their children is known as a
items.explanation: A nuclear family consists of a father, a mother and their children, while an extended family includes other relatives such as grandparents.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Social Studies and Civic Education

items.stem: Which of the following is a basic human right of every Nigerian child?
options: The right to refuse to go to school
The right to drive a car
The right to vote in elections
items.explanation: Every child has the right to basic education, which is provided for in the constitution and in the Child Rights Act.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Social Studies and Civic Education

items.stem: The process by which adult citizens choose their leaders through voting is called an
items.explanation: An election is the process by which qualified adult citizens vote to choose their leaders or representatives.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Social Studies and Civic Education

items.stem: Which of the following is the best way to prevent the spread of malaria in a community?
options: Drinking dirty water from the stream
Sleeping without a net near stagnant water
Draining stagnant water and using treated nets
items.explanation: Malaria is spread by mosquitoes that breed in stagnant water, so draining such water and using treated nets reduce the spread.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Social Studies and Civic Education

items.stem: A person who lives in a country and enjoys its rights while performing its duties is called a
items.explanation: A citizen is a legal member of a country who enjoys its rights and is expected to perform civic duties.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Social Studies and Civic Education

items.stem: Which of the following national symbols represents the authority and identity of the Nigerian state?
items.explanation: The national flag is a symbol of the nation's authority and identity, and it is flown on official occasions.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Social Studies and Civic Education

items.stem: A pupil sees a stranger offering sweets to younger children near the school gate. What is the most responsible action for the pupil to take?
options: Report the stranger to a teacher at once
items.explanation: Reporting the stranger to a teacher promptly helps protect the younger children from possible harm.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Social Studies and Civic Education

items.stem: The type of government in which the people rule through their elected representatives is called
items.explanation: Democracy is a system of government in which the people rule either directly or through their elected representatives.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Social Studies and Civic Education

items.stem: Which of the following is a social institution that is mainly responsible for the upbringing of children?
items.explanation: The family is the basic social institution that first cares for and brings up children and teaches them values.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Social Studies and Civic Education

items.stem: A trader refuses to sell his goods to a customer because of the customer's tribe. This behaviour is an example of
items.explanation: Treating someone unfairly because of their tribe is discrimination, which is wrong and is prohibited by law.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Social Studies and Civic Education

items.stem: Which of the following is the correct way for a pedestrian to cross a busy road?
options: Cross the road while reading a book
Use the pedestrian bridge or zebra crossing
Wave at the drivers and walk slowly
items.explanation: Pedestrians should cross at a pedestrian bridge or zebra crossing, where drivers expect them and the risk of accident is lowest.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Social Studies and Civic Education

items.stem: The study of how people earn and spend money and how goods are produced and distributed is called
items.explanation: Economics studies how people earn and spend money and how goods and services are produced, distributed and consumed.
items.reference: BECE Syllabus - Social Studies and Civic Education
